subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the difference between quality control and quality assurance?
options: Quality control happens only after sale
Quality control checks products at the end; quality assurance builds quality into the whole process
questions.explain: Quality control inspects finished goods, while quality assurance builds quality in at every stage.

questions.q: Which of these is a fixed cost?
questions.explain: Rent does not change with output, so it is a fixed cost.

questions.q: Job production is best described as:
options: Making identical products on a continuous line
Producing one-off, customised products to a specific order
Making products in groups or sets
questions.explain: Job production makes single, often customised items, such as a tailored suit or a bridge.

options: Output produced per unit of input (e.g. per worker) in a given time
The total amount of stock held
questions.explain: Productivity measures output per input, such as the number of units produced per worker per hour.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of e-commerce for a business?
options: It allows the business to sell to customers 24 hours a day across a wide area
It always removes the need for marketing
It limits sales to local customers only
questions.explain: E-commerce lets a business sell online around the clock to a much larger geographic market.

questions.q: What is a drawback of holding too much stock (overstocking)?
options: Money tied up in stock and higher storage and waste costs
questions.explain: Holding excess stock ties up cash and increases storage, insurance and potential wastage costs.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Profit and cash are the same thing
Profit is always paid in cash immediately
Customers may pay later while the business must pay its own bills now
questions.explain: Profit and cash differ in timing; a firm can be profitable yet short of cash if money comes in slowly.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of strong branding for a business?
options: It allows the business to charge higher prices and build customer loyalty
It removes the need for any marketing
questions.explain: A strong brand builds customer loyalty and often allows a business to charge a premium price.

questions.q: What does TQM (Total Quality Management) involve?
options: Every employee taking responsibility for quality
Checking quality only at the end of production
Only the quality team checking products
questions.explain: TQM is an approach where everyone in the business is responsible for maintaining quality.

questions.q: Qualitative market research data is most useful for understanding:
options: Exactly how many units were sold
questions.explain: Qualitative data explores opinions and reasons behind customer behaviour rather than just numbers.

options: Using data that already exists, such as published reports
questions.explain: Secondary research uses existing data such as government statistics or market reports.

questions.q: Flow production is most suitable for:
options: Mass-producing large quantities of identical, standardised products
questions.explain: Flow (mass) production continuously makes large quantities of identical products, e.g. cars or canned drinks.
